questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 11 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area of a closed cylinder = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r+h). Here that's 2×3.14×5×(5+11) = 502.4 cm². A common mistake is forgetting one circular end (giving 345.4) or leaving out the circles entirely (628.0, which is just the curved surface doubled incorrectly).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's use of proportional representation meant even small parties could win seats in parliament. Why did this make government harder?
options: It often produced weak coalition governments that struggled to agree and act decisively
It meant only the Kaiser's party could ever win seats
It gave the army automatic control of parliament
It made elections illegal after 1919
questions.answer: It often produced weak coalition governments that struggled to agree and act decisively
questions.why: Proportional representation gave many small parties seats, so no single party had a majority. Governments were fragile coalitions that frequently collapsed, making stable decision-making difficult — this is different from confusing PR with banning elections or removing civilian power.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best shows the causal chain linking the Great Depression to the Nazi Party's growth, rather than just noting they occurred at the same time?
options: Mass unemployment from the Depression made Nazi promises of jobs and strong leadership newly appealing to desperate voters
The Depression happened, and separately the Nazis also became more popular around then
The Depression proved Hitler was right about everything from the start
The Depression only affected farmers, who never voted Nazi
questions.answer: Mass unemployment from the Depression made Nazi promises of jobs and strong leadership newly appealing to desperate voters
questions.why: A causal link requires showing mechanism: economic despair drove people toward parties offering radical solutions and stability. Simply noting the timing overlap (option 2) isn't causation, and the other options misrepresent the actual historical pattern.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Two students argue about Australia's post-WWII migration. One says 'people only came because Australia was desperate for workers.' The other says 'people only came to escape hardship at home.' What's the better historical view?
options: Both push and pull factors worked together — hardship abroad and Australia's need for labour and population both mattered
Only push factors mattered; Australia's own needs were irrelevant
Only pull factors mattered; conditions overseas were irrelevant
Migration in this period was entirely random with no identifiable factors
questions.answer: Both push and pull factors worked together — hardship abroad and Australia's need for labour and population both mattered
questions.why: Migration is best explained by combining push factors (like postwar hardship in Europe) with pull factors (like Australia's assisted passage schemes and labour shortages). Picking only one side oversimplifies a two-sided process.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student writing a business plan for a new car wash wants to include a SWOT analysis. Which of these belongs correctly inside the SWOT section, rather than the market analysis section?
options: The business has low startup costs but faces threat from three nearby competitors
Local car ownership rates are rising in this suburb
Competitors currently charge between $15 and $25 for a wash
Weekly traffic counts on the main road are increasing
questions.answer: The business has low startup costs but faces threat from three nearby competitors
questions.why: SWOT covers internal Strengths/Weaknesses and external Opportunities/Threats about the business itself. Facts about market size, competitor pricing, or customer numbers describe the external market and belong in market analysis, not SWOT.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When a pathogen invades the body, memory cells 'remember' it so future infections are fought off faster. What is this ability called?
options: Immunity
Digestion
Photosynthesis
Respiration
questions.why: Immunity is the body's ability to resist a pathogen it has previously encountered, thanks to memory cells that allow a faster antibody response next time. This is distinct from unrelated body processes like digestion or respiration.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A migrant moves permanently from Vietnam to Australia to reunite with family already living there. Which term correctly describes this kind of movement?
options: International migration
Urbanisation
Internal migration
Emigration only, with no pull factor involved
questions.why: International migration is the permanent movement of people across national borders. Urbanisation refers to movement from rural to urban areas usually within a country, and internal migration also stays within one country — neither fits crossing from Vietnam to Australia.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 15 cm and a height of 7 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
options: 52.5 cm²
105 cm²
22 cm²
45.5 cm²
questions.why: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 15 × 7 = 52.5 cm². Forgetting to halve gives 105 cm² — the classic rushing mistake. Slowing down to say the formula first stops that error.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 12 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2×3.14×9 + 2×3.14×3×12 = 56.5 + 226.1 = 282.6 cm². Missing one end circle gives 226.1, and using only curved surface doubled incorrectly gives other wrong totals.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Why is the Weimar Republic sometimes described as facing a 'crisis of legitimacy' from its very first years?
options: Many Germans blamed it for accepting the humiliating Treaty of Versailles, even though it wasn't the government that started the war
It was actually a monarchy pretending to be a republic
It had no elections at all, so nobody supported it
It was created by Hitler to gain early popularity
questions.answer: Many Germans blamed it for accepting the humiliating Treaty of Versailles, even though it wasn't the government that started the war
questions.why: The Weimar government signed the Treaty of Versailles and was unfairly blamed for Germany's defeat and humiliation, even though the Kaiser's government had led the war. This 'stab-in-the-back' resentment undermined public trust from the start.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best shows why rising unemployment during the Great Depression benefited the Nazis more than other struggling parties?
options: The Nazis offered a clear, radical solution (blame and strong leadership) that felt decisive compared to the weak coalition governments people blamed for the crisis
The Nazis were the only party allowed to campaign during the Depression
Unemployment had no real effect on which party people supported
The Depression made every party equally popular
questions.answer: The Nazis offered a clear, radical solution (blame and strong leadership) that felt decisive compared to the weak coalition governments people blamed for the crisis
questions.why: The Nazis specifically benefited because their message of strong, decisive leadership and scapegoating contrasted with the perceived weakness of coalition governments — this is a specific mechanism, not just general dissatisfaction spreading evenly across all parties.
